html:
Anguilla was formally separated from the colony of Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla in December 1980 and became a British dependency of its own. Britain had grouped the three islands for most of a century and a half.

The step closed the dispute opened by the Anguilla Revolution and Operation Sheepskin. It also cleared the way for the independence of St Kitts and Nevis in 1983, without Anguilla.

Since then Anguilla has lived mainly from tourism and offshore finance, under a governor sent from London and an elected local government within the British overseas territories.
